calls.head: Penalties could cost the Sharks
calls.body: The Sharks’ penalty kill sits 24th in the league, and the Oilers’ power play is 1st (9.5 expected goals per 60). Discipline matters more than usual for the Sharks tonight.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.5 expected goals per 60.

calls.happened: Edmonton’s power play created 16.6 expected goals per 60 in 4:00 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 9.5, and scored 0 goals.
calls.beyond: Edmonton’s power play created 16.6 expected goals per 60, against their usual 9.5 and a league average of 7.5. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

calls.head: The Sharks’ goalie is in for some dangerous shots
calls.body: The Oilers make their shots count (10th in the league: a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot), and the Sharks are 29th at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Oilers to get some real chances.
calls.call: The Oilers’ average shot has at least their usual 6.6% chance of going in.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season
calls.happened: Edmonton’s average shot had a 6.4% chance of going in, against their usual 6.6%.

calls.head: Bodies will fly
calls.body: The Oilers have a hit score of 110 (8th in the league) and the Sharks 116 (4th), where 100 is league average after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.
calls.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 113.

calls.happened: The two teams’ combined hit score was 137, against their usual 113 (100 is league average, after adjusting for the arena’s scorer).
calls.beyond: San Jose’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 172, against their usual 116 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

calls.head: Don’t blink and you still might miss the shots
calls.body: Edmonton plays some of the league’s slowest games (24th for pace: 80.1 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined), and so does San Jose (29th). We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at fewer than 78.3 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, slower than either team’s usual.

calls.happened: The game ran at 62.3 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the slower team’s usual 78.3 and a league average of 81.7.

SJS.head: We gave San Jose only a 32% chance, and it went the way we feared.

EDM.head: We gave Edmonton a 68% chance, and Edmonton delivered.

surprises.head: San Jose couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: San Jose’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 3.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 150 games.

surprises.head: San Jose tried a different line
surprises.body: M. Celebrini, M. Marchment, W. Smith played 11:39 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of San Jose’s usual lines.

story.head: The Oilers beat the Sharks
paras: Mattias Ekholm opened the scoring midway through the first. Vasily Podkolzin scored the winner early in the third.

The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Oilers win about seven in ten. By our Swing measure, Connor McDavid had the best night of anyone. The Sharks tried a line they hadn’t used before: Macklin Celebrini, Mason Marchment and Will Smith.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Oilers.
Connor McDavid has a point in every game this season.
Mattias Ekholm scored his first goal of the season.
Whether the Sharks keep that line together at home against Boston on Tuesday.
